public_observations.text: GSEM formalizes clinical experience with applicable-condition context and indication/contraindication polarity and identifies Boundary Failure as partial-condition transfer that ignores applicability boundaries. Its paper retrieval ablation reports GSEM 94.22/94.59/34 versus 92.71/92.57/24 without entity recall, 93.62/83.78/10 without embedding recall, and 91.79/92.57/23 without multi-seed retrieval.

The checked current paper-linked GSEM implementation asks an LLM to collect a node when its condition/context is relevant or partially relevant to the query and also says at least one experience must be collected. This is relevance-based selection rather than an inspectable mandatory boundary-satisfaction predicate.

The checked current GSEM multi-start implementation forces fallback-to-start for every valid seed path that selected no memory. A path therefore cannot preserve an all-rejected empty memory result once a valid start seed exists.

The same public repository exposes a GSEMMultiStartNoFillAgent explicitly described as multi-start traversal without per-start fallback-to-start. The inspected paper Table 3 does not report this factor and no numeric no-fill result was established in the checked current public surfaces, so its causal effect remains unresolved.

TAG is a direct general-domain post-retrieval control precedent: a memory-conditioned second pass must exceed baseline confidence by a margin and pass deterministic structural guards or the system rolls back to the baseline. Its locked training-free protocol reports +7.0 SVAMP and +7.67 ASDiv points over baseline and includes fixed-retrieval counterfactual evidence.

QCR holds candidate retrieval, target state, model, decoding and tool budget fixed while changing how the same selected trajectory is delivered. Across 2,391 WebArena/WorkArena/AppWorld targets it reaches 62.3% success, 10.7 points above Full Trajectory with 48.9% fewer online tokens, supporting post-retrieval reuse as a separable causal axis.

protocol_inferences.name: APPLICABILITY_GATE_MUST_PRESERVE_ABSTENTION
protocol_inferences.text: When every candidate is rejected/held by receiver applicability logic, runtime must permit an empty memory set. Forced fallback-to-one-memory converts rejection into authority.

protocol_inferences.name: RELEVANCE_IS_NOT_APPLICABILITY
protocol_inferences.text: Relevance/partial relevance may nominate a candidate but cannot prove all boundary or contraindication predicates are satisfied.

protocol_inferences.name: POST_RETRIEVAL_CONTROL_IS_A_SEPARATE_CAUSAL_AXIS
protocol_inferences.text: Claims about receiver reuse/admission should hold candidate retrieval identity fixed where possible rather than confounding retrieval quality with applicability control.

protocol_inferences.name: REJECTED_MEMORY_MUST_ROLL_BACK_OR_ABSTAIN
protocol_inferences.text: A rejected memory must roll back to an independently valid baseline action or leave memory empty; it must not silently fall through to forced injection.

protocol_probe.name: failure_memory_admission_abstention_probe_20260829
protocol_probe.purpose: Additive checker for the new abstention-preservation lifecycle invariant without mutating the canonical failure-memory v2 validator.

residual_dependency_findings: GSEM, TAG and QCR all depend on model/tool execution and are mechanism evidence rather than zero-dependency scheduled-Chat completion routes.
GSEM's checked current public normal retriever does not fail closed after all candidate rejections because it forces a start-node fallback.
TAG/QCR strengthen post-retrieval causal separation but are not autonomous-science matched applicability-gate experiments.
